parallel.requirements: Recognized the required ESM .mjs output, manual process.argv parsing, no external dependencies, split modules, and furl-like scheme/host/path/query output behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept primary implementation ownership but also spawned a behavior-probing child in the same shared workspace; both agents ultimately wrote deliverable files.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote an initial argparse_compat/query_codec/url_reference/furl_like/python_print/test6.mjs set, while the child wrote argv_parser/query_string/furl_like/test6.mjs; the final active tree used the child-style files after parent edits.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration required parent inspection of unexpected active files, acceptance of a mixed tree, edits to child-authored modules, and deletion of the parent-only helper modules before delivering test6.mjs.
parallel.verification: The parent ran executable-versus-node comparison scripts and reported all comparison cases matched after reconciling the active file set.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed the submitted artifact at 127 of 163 cases, so local verification did not cover every hidden furl/argparse behavior.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, manual argv, no dependency, split-module, and black-box executable matching requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final response without delegation or shared workspace ownership conflict.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote a coherent module set: cli.mjs, python-print.mjs, query-codec.mjs, query.mjs, url-parts.mjs, furl.mjs, and test6.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The single agent assembled the entrypoint against its own library modules and delivered those files as the final artifact tree.
serial.verification: The serial run compared node output with the executable across ordinary URL cases, parser errors, help handling, duplicate flags, equals form, negative values, spaces, and malformed query cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed the submitted artifact at 123 of 163 cases, with hidden cases beyond the locally checked behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required Python behavior and Node constraints from the prompt, including ESM .mjs files, manual argv parsing, and no external packages.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same task obligations and treated the executable as the black-box oracle for parser and furl behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is visible; both attempted the same migration and both missed hidden official cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work by spawning a behavior-probing child, but both parent and child ended up writing implementation files in the final output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all work under one actor, with multi-agent disabled and zero child threads.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel ownership boundary was overlapping rather than cleanly partitioned; serial had a single implementation owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child brief is redacted in raw evidence, but the observable interface problem is concrete: both agents produced files with the same entrypoint/module responsibilities in one workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent brief, handoff, or component contract because the same actor wrote and consumed all modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel required cross-agent coordination of final artifact ownership and file namespaces; serial avoided that boundary entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implementation shifted from the parent-written helper set to child-style argv_parser/query_string/furl_like modules, then the parent patched those active modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one coherent set of cli, query, URL, furl, print, and entrypoint modules in a single apply_patch operation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel implementation provenance changed mid-run because of overlapping writes; serial implementation provenance stayed stable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent did not simply receive a finished child result; it waited, interrupted the child, and consumed child side effects already written into /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and proceeded from local probing to local implementation and local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result handling occurred through shared filesystem side effects and reconciliation, while serial had no join or child-result stage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had a concrete shared-state conflict: active /output/test6.mjs and furl_like.mjs were child-style files after the parent had written different files, forcing parent reconciliation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and integrated one consistent final tree without another actor changing the files in place.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the central task-solving difference: parallel had unstable final-tree provenance, while serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local executable comparisons before and after reconciliation and reported all comparison cases matched.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local executable comparisons, including broad parser and URL cases, and reported the checked cases passed after fixing shell quoting.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had substantial local verification but neither covered all official hidden cases; parallel's local verification happened around a changed active file tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed without timeout but spent more agent time, more tool calls, and a child interrupt plus reconciliation path before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed without timeout, with fewer tool calls and no child interruption or shared-write repair.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel coordination added overhead and cleanup but did not prevent completion; both final submissions remained official failures.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluations are both failures: parallel passed 127 of 163 samples and serial passed 123 of 163. The visible task-solving contrast is not a pass/fail split but a process difference: parallel had overlapping parent and child writes to the submitted entrypoint and shared URL module, then parent reconciliation; serial had one coherent writer. The score gap is small and does not prove that the overwrite explains any hidden evaluator case.
parallel_contributors: Parallel had an adverse deliverable overwrite and reconciliation episode in the shared /output tree.
Parallel still performed local executable comparisons and ended with a slightly higher official score than serial.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided child coordination and wrote one coherent module set.
Serial also failed official hidden cases despite broad local verification.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations approximated furl and argparse behavior and missed hidden evaluator cases outside their local comparison suites.
The official score difference is a task-behavior difference but not a discordant outcome.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No pass/fail outcome difference; the retained pattern is an evidenced adverse parallel process consequence, not an exclusive root cause for the official both-fail result.

Although the child explored broad behavior, it wrote usable deliverables; the downstream problem was overlapping writes, not unfinished work from an oversized child assignment.
The child brief is redacted and does not prove omission of a known requirement; the child produced relevant implementation artifacts rather than unusable work from missing task context.
There is no separate component-interface incompatibility to classify; live agents wrote the same deliverable and overlapping module, so the concrete write label takes precedence.
No known finding or constraint is shown as lost during transfer; the parent dealt with current files rather than a missing transferred fact.

No conflicting reports or contracts remained unadjudicated; the observed conflict was concrete file replacement and reconciliation.

candidates.reason: The child was interrupted only after it had written deliverable files and after the parent had a local candidate; the realized harm is better captured by the deliverable overwrite and reconciliation.
A final artifact was placed and delivered; the issue was not a complete candidate left unpromoted before closure.
The parent re-ran comparison checks after modifying the active files, so no unverified post-check merge is directly evidenced.
The child implementation was visible in /output and was reconciled into the active final tree rather than ignored or left unjoined.
No verifier child with a trapped concrete finding is present; the only child wrote implementation artifacts.
After interrupting the child, the parent inspected, reconciled, and took over the active files; there was no abandoned required failed child scope.
No completed child result was returned and then ignored; the parent acted on the visible child-written files.
The parent used wait and list/interrupt operations and inspected current files; it did not blindly wait until timeout or closure.
Overlapping file scope existed, but the same episode includes direct replacement of the required entrypoint, so Deliverable Overwrite is more specific.
Same-file collision is a near match, but the same-file collision involved the submitted test6.mjs entrypoint, making Deliverable Overwrite the correct higher-precedence label.
A non-entry module was also overwritten, but the same episode replaced the submitted entrypoint, so Deliverable Overwrite takes precedence over Source Overwrite.

candidates.near_match_reason: Same-File Collision describes a generic same-source collision, but this episode replaced the required executable entrypoint test6.mjs, so Deliverable Overwrite is more specific.

candidates.reason: The parent cleanup removed unused helper files after reconciliation; there is no broader build or promotion replacing the final tree beyond the entrypoint/module overwrite episode.

retained_patterns.reason: The parent wrote the submitted entrypoint and libraries, the child independently wrote another submitted entrypoint and overlapping furl_like module into the same /output tree, and the parent later observed and reconciled the unexpected active deliverable.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parent had to inspect an unexpected active /output tree, patch child-style deliverable modules, and delete its own prior helper files before final delivery.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Same-File Collision is less specific because the overwritten same file was the required submitted entrypoint, which the taxonomy treats as a deliverable.
